title: Ops: require incident taxonomy + owner confirmation in on-call templates/checklists
author: Kira Thompson
release_notes: Internal-only: on-call incident templates now require incident_type/subtype and owner confirmation; adds links to taxonomy decision tree + dashboards and updates the IC checklist to capture SLA timer state.
description: Context: As part of the Reliability Program “Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping”, we’re making incident_type/subtype and owner explicit/required in incident tooling. Incident-bot enforcement is landing separately; this PR updates the in-repo on-call templates/checklists so humans follow the same workflow and we get consistent artifacts even when the bot is bypassed (manual incident docs, retroactive writeups, etc.). What changed: 1) Incident commander checklist now includes an explicit “Classify incident” step (incident_type + subtype) with a link to the v1 decision tree and guidance for multi-cause incidents (pick a primary type; capture others under contributing_systems). 2) New required fields in incident doc templates: incident_type, incident_subtype, customer_tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), primary_owner_team, consulted_teams, and “SLA timer state” (started/paused/override + reason). 3) Adds a short “Owner confirmation” step: IC must confirm primary owner in-channel after incident_type is set; if ownership is disputed, page primary owner per mapping and record dispute in the incident log. 4) Standardizes unknown/unclassified handling: use incident_type=unknown only during active triage; must be resolved before close and/or before postmortem is marked “ready for review”. 5) Adds quick links in templates to the taxonomy dashboards, routing/fleet failover runbooks, and the postmortem template section where taxonomy fields are reviewed. Notes/constraints: - These templates are used by ops-toolkit (internal) to generate the initial incident doc in Confluence; we keep the field names aligned with incident-bot payload fields (incident_type, incident_subtype, owner_team) to avoid translation/duplication. - We intentionally keep the taxonomy fields low-cardinality; templates only allow top-level type + subtype (no freeform tags beyond contributing notes). - Security incidents: templates include a reminder that suspicious auth failures may require dual-tracking with Security Ops; do not paste sensitive indicators into the incident doc. Validation: - Manual: generated an incident doc from template and verified required fields render in the IC section + postmortem stub. - CI: bazel/test + markdown lint. Follow-ups: - Once incident-bot enforcement is fully rolled out, we should deprecate the older “incident-summary.md” template to reduce drift (tracked in ENG-4822). - Add a small pre-submit check in ops-toolkit to fail generation if required fields are missing (tracked in ENG-4829). References: - Confluence: Incident taxonomy v1 definitions + decision tree (eng-sre/reliability-initiatives) - Ownership mapping + remediation SLA matrix - Slack: #eng-sre announcement thread for enforcement rollout

ops/checklists: update IC checklist to include taxonomy classification + owner confirmation
ops/templates: document unknown/unclassified rules and SLA timer state capture
ops: link templates to taxonomy dashboards and relevant runbooks
lint: fix markdownlint issues after template updates
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Please make it unambiguous that incident_type=unknown is allowed only while actively triaging; we should require updating before marking Resolved/Closed. Also add a line about how to handle multi-cause incidents (capacity + routing).

Kira Thompson (author): Updated the IC checklist and incident doc template: clarified unknown only during triage; added a “Primary type vs contributing factors” note and a pointer to the decision tree section on multi-cause incidents.

Allison Grant (review): +1 overall. Small ask: ensure the template doesn’t encourage freeform tags that will later become metric labels. Can we keep this strictly type/subtype + a freeform notes section?
Kira Thompson (author): Done. Removed “tags:” from the template and replaced with “contributing_systems (freeform notes, not labels)”. Also added a warning about metric label cardinality.

Aisha Bello (review): Template mentions SLA timer state—can we explicitly call out start time source (incident declared time) and that pauses require reason? This will help when we wire the evaluator.

Kira Thompson (author): Added “SLA timer state” block with required fields: started_at (declared_at), paused (yes/no), pause_reason, override (yes/no), override_reason, and link to ENG-4829 policy doc.
Dylan Brooks (review): Minor: the field name should be owner_team (matching incident-bot) not primary_owner_team. You can still display it as “Primary owner” in the doc.
Kira Thompson (author): Renamed to owner_team and adjusted headings to “Primary owner (owner_team)”.
Rafael Mendes (approval): Looks good. This will reduce drift between human workflow and bot enforcement. Approved.
